root_cause.text: The functions `drbd_adm_dump_devices()` and `drbd_adm_dump_peer_devices()` in the DRBD subsystem jump to the `put_result` error path (which executes `rcu_read_unlock()`) when a resource lookup fails, without first acquiring the RCU read lock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that when `!resource` is true, `rcu_read_lock()` is explicitly added before jumping to `goto put_result;` in both `drbd_adm_dump_devices()` and `drbd_adm_dump_peer_devices()`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The functions `drbd_adm_dump_devices()` and `drbd_adm_dump_peer_devices()` introduced in this commit both contain the vulnerable logic. Specifically, in `drbd_adm_dump_devices()`, if `drbd_find_resource()` fails (returns NULL), the code executes `goto put_result;` (lines 3127-3128) before calling `rcu_read_lock()` (line 3133). The `put_result` block falls through to `out:`, which executes `rcu_read_unlock()` (line 3180), resulting in an unbalanced RCU unlock. The exact same pattern is present in `drbd_adm_dump_peer_devices()` (lines 3433-3434, 3438, and 3497).
